newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Swiss firm to start trading in Belgian options.
newsitem.headline: Swiss firm to start trading in Belgian options.

text.p: Swiss firm Transoptions S.A. has decided to become a market maker in Bel 20 options from October 1, the Belgian Futures and Options Exchange (Belfox) said in a statement.
Bel-20 is an index of leading Belgian shares.

"The volume in options traded on the Bel 20 seemed appealing and favourable to the arrival of a new market maker. Furthermore, we anticipate trading other Belfox products within the next few months," said Karl Stocklin, general manager of Transoptions, in a statement.
Jos Schmitt, president of Belfox, said Transoptions would contribute to further boost liquidity of the Bel 20 options.
It would also allow Belfox to establish itself in Switzerland, he added.

Transoptions, which is specialised in the market making of of derivatives on automated markets, is a subsidiary of France's Banque de Gestion Privee, which in turn is owned by Caisse Nationale du Credit Agricole and Credit Agricole d'Ile de France.
It is a market maker in derivatives on Deutsche Borse A.G. and Switzerland's SOFFEX, and a member of the Zurich Stock Exchange.
